analyzed_vuln.description: Heap OOB read is caused by insufficient bounds validation before reading DNS answer fields. In the DNS reply path, search_valid_dns checks `if((x+6) >= payload_len) break;` before parsing an RR, then advances `x` by `getNameLength(...)` and immediately calls `rsp_type = get16(&x, payload)` without re-checking that at least 2 bytes remain at the new `x`. With crafted/truncated name encoding, `x` can become equal/near end-of-buffer and `get16` performs an unchecked 2-byte read (`*(u_int16_t*)&payload[*i]`), triggering the ASan heap-buffer-overflow at dns.c:40.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: From fuzz_process_packet, attacker-controlled packet bytes are passed directly to ndpi_detection_process_packet -> ndpi_search_dns -> search_valid_dns. Input must be recognized as DNS over TCP/UDP (ports/heuristics satisfied) and pass initial header-length check. In reply parsing (`flags` indicates response and counts look plausible), a malformed/truncated answer section causes `x` to move near the payload end after name-length handling; because no post-update bounds check exists before `get16`, the function reads 2 bytes past the heap buffer.
